tina.purpose: SSOT architecture model: module/service/contract inventory AND the runtime data plane (carriers, ownership, flows, egress boundary). gate:dataflow enforces model<->disk completeness, single-writer + render-only ownership, and a reality diff against code; gate:calm validates it against the FINOS meeting-intelligence pattern.
tina.principle: P23 — one writer per data carrier; readers never re-derive a producer's data; the model covers every module/service/contract (no drift).

nodes.name: deploy
nodes.description: Deployment and execution-target registry. Local tina CLI/TUI shares Compose configuration, build/activation and readiness logic; operational mutations target the selected Docker context/project, preserve data volumes and support dry-run. Read-only full diagnostics resolve effective ASR through Identity and probe configured host/container health without inference. Allowlisted repository checks reuse existing gates and write private local logs. ASR configuration uses existing Identity global/account settings APIs with explicit scoped previews and secret-free output. Fresh local setup creates private configuration and new Compose-managed volumes, refuses existing configuration/resources and occupied ports, and reuses deployment plus optional ASR configuration/status verification; it does not install native capture or models. No user meeting/agent API client is added.

nodes.name: agent-api
nodes.description: unit control-plane; dispatch -> runtime spawn; meeting copilot Per-user ChatGPT disconnect keeps TINA/ASR sessions separate. Terminal OAuth state is cancelled locally; authenticated internal Agent API owns profile writes, disconnect and generation checks under the same file lock as token refresh. Credentials stay in the private auth volume; callbacks from a disconnected generation cannot restore an old account. Existing in-flight workers may retain short-lived tokens. Owner-scoped meeting Q&A reads canonical transcript and explicitly selected linked private Wiki documents, validates source IDs, stores source fingerprints, and creates a new Wiki page only after explicit Apply; existing pages and canonical data are never overwritten. Routine files are owner-scoped active private-workspace resources: anchored no-symlink I/O, per-owner serialized reconcile, source SHA preconditions for explicit Edit/toggle/delete, and stable IDs per workspace/file. Delete removes the source before cancelling all related jobs; shared workspace files never grant schedules. Chat dispatch serializes configuration changes per thread in Redis using expiring locks and keyed model-configuration digests under agent:chat-config:*. Raw credentials are never stored in that metadata. An unchanged configuration reuses its warm worker; changed provider, credential or model waits for the previous turn-complete and requests cooperative stop through the existing chat input stream, confirms terminal state through runtime.v1 and replaces the idle workload before pre-delivering and spawning the next turn. Busy or unverifiable refreshes return actionable errors without sending the prompt to an old provider. The existing thread id, output stream and provider-session history are preserved. Bedrock model discovery reads paginated regional foundation-model/inference-profile lists; credential tests use native InvokeModel. The API image packages the same Python provider helpers and automatic thinking policy as the worker. All providers use automatic thinking; legacy effort pins are ignored, and the settings UI exposes no manual thinking field. Worker configuration digests include the deployed provider-adapter revision, so adapter fixes replace old warm workers without discarding conversation history. Gemini defaults to gemini-3.5-flash. Gemini, DeepSeek and Bedrock credential tests verify native function-call/result round trips before reporting success; Bedrock uses the same InvokeModelWithResponseStream protocol as its CLI and decodes complete AWS event-stream frames with checksum validation; custom API model registration supplies exact model IDs to the pinned CLI SDK rather than embedding endpoint URIs. Groq credential tests verify a real function-call/result round trip through the worker request adapter before testing summaries. Model discovery excludes speech-only Orpheus entries and marks known text-only ALLaM as summary-only, preventing chat selection while preserving meeting use. Explicit /research chat commands and document research requests resolve a private writable note destination from the authenticated active set. Private Codex history restores turn-scoped recorded source metadata and original opened URLs; missing reference mappings remain visibly unresolved.

nodes.name: configured completion provider
nodes.description: the deployment or per-user model endpoint; may be tenant-hosted or an external provider. Groq uses Codex Responses at https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 for chat, DeepSeek uses the Claude Code Anthropic-compatible endpoint at https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic, and Gemini uses agy with its Gemini API-key provider. Their tool-less meeting jobs use OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions at the respective fixed Groq, DeepSeek and Gemini endpoints. The same masked per-user/platform provider credential selects both paths; TINA transcript API tokens remain separate.

nodes.name: transcription
nodes.description: transcription — OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/transcriptions boundary with selectable backends: faster-whisper/CTranslate2, Apple MLX/Metal, and loopback FunASR Qwen3-ASR with FSMN-VAD. Clients send bounded audio windows, continuity prompts and content-free capture-lag metadata. FunASR exposes asr-status.v1 with actual device, bounded request timing samples, queue and model percentiles; Terminal reads it through a verified admin proxy. Browser render timings remain local. Does not write any redis carrier (the bot XADDs segments). Optional native Rust backend runs Silero VAD and Qwen3-ASR-0.6B INT8 through sherpa-onnx on CPU at host loopback :18001; it preserves VAD segment offsets and the same ASR status contract. The FunASR adapter forwards min_silence_duration_ms to FSMN max_end_silence_time (100-2000 ms, default 800 ms, explicitly pinned), preserving per-VAD sentence offsets for downstream alignment. An isolated single-source Apple Silicon PoC under deploy/transcription/streaming-poc validates real Qwen Transformers decoder token callbacks and paced growing-window hypotheses on cached VI/EN evaluation clips. It is not a selected production endpoint, does not claim an incremental audio encoder, and never changes/restarts production services; private external artifacts record token timing, accuracy, RAM and before/after listener identities. Sub-200 ms FunASR inputs receive trailing silence only in the temporary inference file to avoid incomplete FSMN frames; source PCM, reported duration and sentence bounds retain the original source interval. Empty input and inference failures remain errors. Optional authenticated loopback :18002 backend composes FunASR FSMN-VAD CPU with hash-pinned Gipformer 1.5 INT8 via Sherpa-ONNX OfflineRecognizer. The root Compose asr profile runs that same CPU service, mounts the pinned model directory and owns host port 18002 while enabled; unload the host LaunchAgent to avoid a port conflict. Existing Custom endpoint settings select it for Desktop/Bot without altering the Qwen platform default. Original VAD sample offsets survive speech slicing; no word timing, prompt conditioning, language detection or token streaming is claimed. One inference plus three bounded waiters, no audio/text in diagnostics. Optional native VieGem-ASR + KenLM endpoint at loopback :18005 uses separately pinned VieGem and EmbeddingGemma 2 assets, PyTorch FP32 on explicit MPS/CPU/CUDA, FSMN on CPU and upstream 4-gram CTC prefix beam decoding. It shares the authenticated bounded HTTP worker with Gipformer; inference is serialized and source VAD offsets stay on the original timeline. Installation does not select the endpoint globally. No incremental streaming, word alignment or automatic transcript polish is claimed; VieGem use is restricted by its non-commercial research license and Gemma terms. Identity also exposes the named viegem backend: administrators configure viegem_url in the platform transcription registry and a dotenvx-encrypted TINA_VIEGEM_TOKEN is injected at deployment startup (legacy database token supported only without that env); native startup decrypts its separate private env file strictly, user preferences select the backend name, and internal Bot/Desktop/dictation resolution carries only its registry-owned endpoint credential. Custom endpoints do not inherit the VieGem platform token; the browser-facing admin settings edge treats that credential as write-only. The source-build entrypoint resolves TINA_VIEGEM_DEVICE=auto to native MPS on Apple Silicon or Docker CUDA on Linux/Windows WSL2. Only the CTC model/encoder uses the GPU; FSMN and KenLM remain CPU. Actual MPS/CUDA compute and authenticated audio must pass before deployment succeeds; no silent CPU fallback. CUDA adds an owned Compose overlay with pinned cu130 wheels and one GPU reservation for inference only. MPS excludes the Docker VieGem profile and stops only the old owned CPU service before binding the same host endpoint; native startup failure attempts to restore that prior service while reporting failure. Explicit cpu remains available. Gipformer and token-free Docker model-install jobs are independent; native setup prepares the same pinned cache before activation. Inference mounts cached weights read-only, runtime tokens come from dotenvx and private keys are not mounted. make-down also removes/stops the owned MPS LaunchAgent. Only a fresh registry receives a VieGem default; existing preferences and foreign worker ownership are preserved. Per-account ASR runtime control keeps shared workers alive while any enabled account requests them. A derived-key authenticated drain fence refuses new requests and cannot stop a worker with active inference. CUDA hardware validation remains pending on a real NVIDIA host.

nodes.name: desktop
nodes.description: all-in-one dev host: bot+collector+gateway in one process; capture sessions resolve central identity ASR settings once (personal API key > platform > environment), pin the selection until stop and expose credential-free backend metadata Local SQLite journal preserves confirmed ASR, PCM source timestamps and owner corrections across restarts; document/review/audio routes consult canAccess. Explicit post-meeting second-pass ASR yields persisted proposals; one worker pauses between utterances for live capture and never edits text before owner Apply.; input ring shared with ASR, per-session/source sample clock and original capture timestamp archived in SQLite; authorized audio-timeline.v1 metadata and RAM-to-archive range reads never fill missing samples; WS /ws fans out transcript.v1 confirmed/pending frames to local capture clients; vi-en pending ASR language reviews archive original/retry text plus source PCM separately from confirmed transcript; owner/origin-checked asr-reviews routes and review UI expose suggestions without adding them to canonical or memory. Ingest ready advertises recording_ack and recording_resume for an optional client_session nonce. REC1 acknowledgements follow sink processing; explicit finalization closes immediately while unexpected socket closes retain the recording assembler for 30 seconds for same-client resume. Shutdown flushes pending assemblers. Different logical client sessions finalize separately; replacing a current recording master preserves the older file as a versioned sibling. Opt-in audio_ack=sample-range.v1 requires indexed PCM and a client_session nonce; exact-range audio-ack follows durable journal insertion. Persistent archive session ids deduplicate identical PCM/timestamps across reconnect and process restart without duplicate pipeline feed; conflicting/overlapping ranges fail without ACK. Socket-local pipeline RAM stays separate from archive identity. Audio ACK does not promise downstream ASR completion. A single background ASR recovery worker resumes unprocessed source/sample ranges after stop or restart, using bounded 15-second archive windows and the existing Gmeet ASR/filter engine. It yields to live capture, retries failures with backoff, pins an opaque backend/credential digest, and never substitutes an unavailable configuration. Owner/origin-scoped asr-recovery.v1 exposes jobs and checkpoints. Recovered mixed audio stays unattributed; known channel names and local mic identity are preserved. Live confirmed segments project accepted canonical text at the gateway; drafts for edited/restored ids are suppressed. transcript.v1 binary/event shapes are unchanged and revision metadata remains on the separate transcript.revised/HTTP interfaces. Owner-only stt-foundation.v1 snapshots persist a journal instance and monotonic sequence; globally stable meeting/source/segment IDs retain exact sample references and accepted revision history. stt-metrics.v1 distinguishes bounded ASR-call, capture lag, SQLite persistence, caption and client-reported foreground UI timing; no text/audio in metrics. Mixed lane transcript IDs include connection and source channel so mic/tab/reconnect turn counters cannot collide. STT diagnostics separate confirmed-caption publication delay from draft-window age; the legacy combined series remains available. Capture teardown plans missing source/sample ranges instead of blanket-checkpointing received PCM; only confirmed or successfully committed recovery ranges advance ASR coverage. Historical checkpoints are preserved. Late accepted PCM atomically reopens completed ASR sessions before ACK so appended tails remain recoverable. Batch archive recovery selects the existing mixed media/repetition filter through the Gmeet host policy hook, retaining short single-word speech while RMS/confidence/language checks remain in force; live Gmeet defaults and completed historical jobs are unchanged. Desktop owns a meeting-local SQLite speaker registry: channel 1000 is one local microphone identity, raw 1002 is archive-only, verified Meet participant IDs bind distinct people, and system mix 999 stays unknown. Owner rename/assignment uses independent speaker revisions and the durable metadata outbox. Owner-triggered post-meeting diarization sends verified saved system audio to the existing authenticated loopback worker; proposals require explicit Apply with registry, text, timeline and audio-hash checks. Manual names/unknown and participant identities are protected. Owner-only canonical and meeting-memory endpoints share accepted speaker projection; drafts/raw mic never become evidence, and words remain segment_fallback without forced alignment. HTTP Window ASR defaults remain unchanged. Owner-triggered post-meeting MFA alignment batches up to 20 verified continuous mono PCM16 clips, at most 30 seconds each, over current accepted text. Alignment jobs yield between batches to live capture and serialize with refinement/diarization. Per-segment accepted timing publishes only after expected text revision, text/audio hashes and capture source references still match. Word audio playback rechecks provenance and never assigns time to OOV tokens. Text edits and Restore invalidate timing atomically. Canonical words/phrases use source-absolute times; speaker attribution is reprojected from the current registry and applied acoustic turns. Alignment types, hashing, validation and speaker projection live in the pure alignment-model module; transcript-journal depends on that model, while the alignment worker depends on the journal, without a runtime import cycle.

nodes.name: meeting-api
nodes.description: collector + bot-spawn + recordings + sessions + calendar import/autojoin (the hub); optionally asks an external service authority before spawn and at one-minute active boundaries. Owns immutable raw ASR plus the transcript_edits overlay with locked expected_revision checks. Owns owner-triggered advisory RMS/clipping/quiet-frame/repetition checks over bounded saved bot audio, check-only jobs without inference, and selective refinement of flagged clips; original transcript remains immutable until explicit Apply. Owns post-meeting recording refinement and optional Vietnamese word alignment over clocked saved audio; alignment/OOV timestamps are a separate owner view and never rewrite transcript-document.v1 or raw ASR. Canonical accepted text/revision and alignment metadata use the transactional JSONB revision outbox; current-text GIN search remains text-only. Owns the durable meeting-local speaker registry, observed Meet participant bindings, owner-confirmed names and assignment history; owner-triggered local CPU diarization applies speaker overlays and word attribution leaves overlap/uncertainty unknown. Persists owner-only canonical-transcript.v1 with current text, source-clock word alignment, speaker attribution and hashes. Incremental meeting-memory.v1 groups finalized speech into conversation windows and exact-quote VI/EN extraction candidates, rebuilt on source revisions; no inferred owner/deadline. Owner-only stt-foundation.v1 native exports and CAS-protected read-only source replicas in meeting.data.stt_replicas retain source authority; replicas never overwrite native Bot canonical rows. Alignment commits atomically reject stale expected_revision; job admission uses expected prior job ID; raw collector upserts cannot overwrite edited rows. Content-free transcript_storage events separate PostgreSQL persistence from Redis mutable-tail queue age.

nodes.description: runtime.v1 kernel: POST /workloads spawns containers (docker/k8s/process) Cron schedules carry an IANA timezone (legacy UTC); local wall-clock boundaries avoid DST arithmetic drift. Atomic Redis claim, cancellation tombstones and completion/retry/rearm publication prevent canceled jobs from recurring, including cancellation of a completed job snapshot whose successor already exists.

nodes.name: agent-worker
nodes.description: spawned isolated workspace-agent worker; selectable Claude Code, Codex app-server, or Antigravity CLI (agy) harness; every dispatch mounts the ordered [_global, active workspaces, _system] stack, fails closed without _global, and loads its authoritative entry context. Groq mode reuses Codex against the fixed Groq Responses endpoint for chat and OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions for meeting summaries. A per-turn Groq model profile disables unsupported freeform patch tools and namespace delegation at the CLI source, with provider-neutral TINA instructions and file edits through the existing sandboxed function tools. DeepSeek mode reuses Claude Code against DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint for chat and its Chat Completions endpoint for summaries. Gemini mode selects agy's Gemini API-key provider for chat and the Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint for summaries, without consumer/OAuth credentials or a synthetic Terms acknowledgment. Dispatch selects each effective per-user/platform key for both paths and clears other providers' credentials. A temporary authenticated loopback proxy inside the worker strips unsupported Responses fields and non-function tools, maps developer instructions to system messages for non-GPT-OSS chat templates without changing tool history, rejects known non-tool chat models, serializes function calls and preserves streamed events and HTTP errors; it never executes tools or expands the harness grants. Codex pins explicit named per-turn filesystem profiles to TINA write grants, protects agent/Git metadata and excludes temporary write roots. Trusted chat/routine turns map WebSearch/WebFetch grants to cached/live hosted web tools; untrusted event/transcription turns disable web tools and remain read-only/offline. Shell networking requires Bash plus WebFetch and a root-owned exclusive GitHub-domain proxy policy, with private addresses, upstream proxies, Unix-socket forwarding and direct-network bypass blocked. Managed networking is not globally forced so offline turns remain isolated. Codex loads workspace instructions and skills, maps TINA auto/gate MCP grants to Codex approval modes, streams tool lifecycle events, pauses gate calls for owner-scoped, one-call decisions over chat streams using tool-approval.v1, and participates in the shared transcript-size resume cap. A private per-TINA-session provider-thread index preserves display history across provider restarts; reset removes this index, and legacy recovery uses only same-subject, same-session Redis events newer than session creation. Codex user-message events define visible human messages, excluding injected environment and developer context; restored tool names remain descriptive. Antigravity maps TINA mount grants to read_file/write_file permissions, sandboxes commands, loads governed skills, exposes only auto-granted non-secret MCP servers in headless mode, and normalizes streamed events and conversation ids. The legacy Antigravity model selection requires a persisted Terms warning acknowledgment; consumer OAuth access through third-party software is prohibited by Google's terms. The Gemini API-key provider has independent credential preflight. Harness-written kg/entities files are workspace.v1-validated before commit. Post-meeting summary uses a tool-less CompletionPort and a deterministic writer with a local generated-content fingerprint, inference-time compare-and-swap, workspace locking and atomic publication; user-edited or unmarked existing documents are preserved, and only the meeting entity path is committed. Meeting Q&A uses a private short-lived, tool-less CompletionPort job with read-only mounts and no public chat history. Web-enabled Codex turns render explicit source metadata as final Markdown links and persist bounded per-turn source records in private continuity; missing citation mappings are never guessed. Explicit Knowledge research instructions create a new private Markdown note with meeting/repo/web source rows, evidence versions and verification dates, preserving other files and canonical transcript/audio.

nodes.name: TINA Capture
nodes.description: Tauri/Rust macOS 15+ client: explicit meeting capture of microphone and system audio plus hold-to-dictate from a global Fn shortcut. Separate source channels are validated, resampled to 16 kHz with SpeexDSP and sent as capture.v1 to local Desktop. Native Capture does not link Sherpa/ONNX for resampling, avoiding incompatible KissFFT symbols between Sherpa and fixed-point Speex. Resampler float samples use PCM16 units internally and return normalized PCM; packet boundaries do not change the output waveform. Default dual-source capture uses Speex AEC plus residual echo suppression with channel 999 as far-end reference, preserves raw mic on archive-only channel 1002 and routes processed mic on channel 1000 to ASR. Aligned dual-source blocks additionally use a stateful 70 Hz high-pass on mic/reference and Speex denoising capped at -3 dB; AGC/VAD remain off and no samples are gated out. TINA_MIC_CLEANUP=0 restores AEC plus residual-only behavior; TINA_SPEEX_RESIDUAL_SUPPRESSION=0 keeps linear AEC only and TINA_SPEEX_AEC=0 uses raw mic. Capture Diagnostics distinguishes configured AEC from actual processed blocks, reports bypassed samples and source mic clipping, and exposes setup fallback reasons without audio or text. Pause/resume clears pending audio and DSP state while retaining session counters. Missing sample-index.v1, DSP initialization failure or unavailable reference passes original mic through. CoreAudio process metadata raises a non-focusable detect/record/ended overlay for allowlisted meeting apps after a 5 s sustain; capture never auto-starts, pause drops frames and freezes the elapsed clock, and a meeting-end reminder offers a 15 s keep-recording grace. Live captions subscribe to Desktop WS /ws, keep a rolling confirmed/pending window for the floating subtitle window, and never affect audio. Markdown export reads the Desktop transcript. Dictation uses microphone only; after stop, Desktop may forward only final transcript text through the authenticated polish bridge, while TINA Capture keeps raw ASR available for copy/restore and pastes raw text if polish is unavailable. No screen images or active-app contents are read; no model or service credentials are loaded in this process.

nodes.name: Desktop transcript journal
nodes.description: Local SQLite WAL: durable meetings, immutable per-source Float32 PCM timeline and original ASR with compare-and-swap correction history. Single writer Desktop. Audio cap 2 GiB/session is surfaced as archive incomplete; ASR continues. Stores refinement jobs/proposals and atomic apply with ASR model/audio hash provenance. Canonical FTS5 current-text index and transactional revision outbox, rebuilt/replayed across restart. Additive asr_language_reviews table stores pending original/retry results and Float32 request audio, deduplicated per meeting/session/PCM hash; 90-second request and 256 MiB per-meeting audio limits. Additive audio_capture_sessions maps meeting/client nonce to persistent archive id; audio_chunks acts as durable exact sample-range receipt with byte/timestamp comparison and overlap rejection. Existing 2 GiB session quota includes pre-restart bytes. Additive asr_sessions, asr_windows and asr_coverage persist routing digests, source/sample jobs and processed intervals; speaker_name is stored with audio chunks. Live confirmed text and its coverage commit atomically. Recovery transcript, FTS index, sample checkpoint and completed job share one SQLite transaction. Running jobs become retryable after process restart. Historical PCM without routing metadata is not auto-decoded. Additive journal_metadata and foundation_versions retain source authority identity and export sequence across restart. Additive speaker_registries, diarization_jobs and canonical_projections persist independent speaker revisions, source-bound proposals and canonical projection versions. Speaker updates and speaker-revision.v1 outbox commit atomically; raw PCM/text remain unchanged. Speaker-aware stt-foundation.v1 exports preserve optional speaker ID/revision. Additive alignment_jobs and alignment_results store accepted-text timing independent from raw ASR; transcript_sequences supplies monotonic metadata invalidation sequences independent of text history length. Alignment result and metadata-only event commit in one SQLite transaction. Original source timestamps and accepted/raw text never change during alignment.

nodes.description: Private .meeting-knowledge/{meeting_id}/{answer_id}.json snapshots and create-only wiki/meetings/{meeting_id}/{answer_id}.md pages. An answer may include up to four additional individually authorized meetings with namespaced sources and source-meeting audio. Retrieval ranks within each meeting and allocates excerpt/character budgets in rounds across meetings with evidence. Related documents resolve aliased, encoded and relative wikilinks after reviewed moves. When a saved Wiki page moves, frontmatter identity locates it in the same visible workspace; locked Apply reuses that page, preserves edited content and refuses ambiguous copies instead of recreating the old path. Missing or revoked meetings redact stored claims and quotes. Source fingerprints are rechecked after inference, on answer review, Apply and Wiki opening; this is cross-store freshness checking, not a distributed transaction. nodes.name: Explicit private Markdown document edits

Reviewed moves preview source-preserving static backlinks and outgoing relative links in the same workspace; confirmation rechecks the full plan fingerprint, preserves code and aliases, reports ambiguous/uneditable references, rolls back ordinary write failures and removes the source last. Bounded Unicode Markdown content search excludes hidden paths and symlinks. Dashboard uses source-preserving formatting, a folder tree, wikilinks, history and per-account/workspace/file draft recovery across reloads via browser session storage retaining the original SHA-256; Terminal searches its authorized active mounts. Explicit per-path Git commit leaves unrelated staged paths and remotes untouched; shared workspaces remain read-only here. General harness writers retain their existing filesystem behavior.

nodes.name: ASR host controller
nodes.description: Local host lifecycle bridge installed by make-all as an owned LaunchAgent on Mac or detached process on WSL2. Terminal verifies its auth cookie and forwards only the current user id with a derived control key. Identity owns per-account enabled/backend/revision preferences and aggregate demand; the controller starts and audio-tests known ASR workers before CAS preference commits. It serializes changes, waits ten idle seconds, conservatively retains both workers while any meeting bot or local Desktop capture exists, drains only with a distinct derived worker key and rechecks demand before stopping an owned Docker service or native MPS LaunchAgent. No arbitrary commands, endpoints, secret values or other user records reach the browser. A private state file records desired backend names and is rebuilt from Identity after restart. make-down stops the controller before shutting down services. Unavailable health or drain checks retain workers rather than force-stop.
